\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ધરપકડ} (dharpakaḍ)}{ધરપકડ (dharpakaḍ)}]{\gu{ધરપકડ} (dharpakaḍ) — an arrest}

\label{lesson:GU-C288-dharpakad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to hide oneself, then the Gujarati for to break (something).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ધરપકડ}}
\textbf{\gu{ધરપકડ}} — \emph{dharpakaḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}an arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{પોલીસે} \gu{ગઈકાલે} \gu{બે} \gu{ચોરોની} \gu{ધરપકડ} \gu{કરી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīse gaīkāle be coronī dharpakaḍ karī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Yesterday the police arrested two thieves.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ધરપકડ}} (\emph{dharpakaḍ}) is built from the stem of \emph{dharvũ}, to hold, from Sanskrit \emph{dhárati} (CDIAL 6747), and \emph{pakaḍ}, a grip, the noun of \textbf{\gu{પકડવું}}: a holding and a seizing. The police \textbf{\gu{ધરપકડ} \gu{કરે} \gu{છે}}, make an arrest.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dharpakaḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dharpakaḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polīse gaīkāle be coronī dharpakaḍ karī.} — Yesterday the police arrested two thieves.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to hide oneself, then the Gujarati for to break (something), then say \emph{dharpakaḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ધરપકડ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An arrest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{કબૂલવું} (kabūlvũ)}{કબૂલવું (kabūlvũ)}]{\gu{કબૂલવું} (kabūlvũ) — to confess}

\label{lesson:GU-C288-kabulvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to break (something), then the Gujarati for an arrest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{કબૂલવું}}
\textbf{\gu{કબૂલવું}} — \emph{kabūlvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to confess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ચોરે} \gu{થાણામાં} \gu{ગુનો} \gu{કબૂલ્યો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{core thāṇāmā̃ guno kabūlyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the police station the thief confessed to the crime.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{ગુનો} \gu{કબૂલ્યો}, \emph{teṇe guno kabūlyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{કબૂલવું}} (\emph{kabūlvũ}) is built on \emph{kabūl}, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{qabūl}, \textquotedblleft{}acceptance\textquotedblright{}: to confess is to accept what you did. \textbf{\gu{ગુનો} \gu{કબૂલ્યો}}, he admitted the crime.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kabūlvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kabūlvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{core thāṇāmā̃ guno kabūlyo.} — At the police station the thief confessed to the crime.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to break (something), then the Gujarati for an arrest, then say \emph{kabūlvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{કબૂલવું} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To confess\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{નકારવું} (nakārvũ)}{નકારવું (nakārvũ)}]{\gu{નકારવું} (nakārvũ) — to deny}

\label{lesson:GU-C288-nakarvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for an arrest, then the Gujarati for to confess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{નકારવું}}
\textbf{\gu{નકારવું}} — \emph{nakārvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to deny\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{પહેલાં} \gu{તેણે} \gu{બધું} \gu{નકાર્યું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pahelā̃ teṇe badhũ nakāryũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At first he denied everything.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{ગુનો} \gu{નકાર્યો}, \emph{teṇe guno nakāryo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{નકારવું}} (\emph{nakārvũ}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{nakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}the word \emph{na}, no\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6907): to deny is to say no to something. You deny a thing: \textbf{\gu{ગુનો} \gu{નકાર્યો}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nakārvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nakārvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pahelā̃ teṇe badhũ nakāryũ.} — At first he denied everything.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for an arrest, then the Gujarati for to confess, then say \emph{nakārvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{નકારવું} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To deny\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગુનેગાર} (gunegār)}{ગુનેગાર (gunegār)}]{\gu{ગુનેગાર} (gunegār) — a criminal}

\label{lesson:GU-C288-gunegar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to confess, then the Gujarati for to deny.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગુનેગાર}}
\textbf{\gu{ગુનેગાર}} — \emph{gunegār} — \textquotedblleft{}a criminal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{ત્યાં} \gu{અજવાળું} \gu{હોત} \gu{તો} \gu{મીરા} \gu{ગુનેગારને} \gu{ઓળખત}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tyā̃ ajvāḷũ hot to Mīrā gunegārne oḷkhat.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there had been light, Mira would have recognized the criminal.
\end{quote}

A masculine or feminine noun, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગુનેગાર}} (\emph{gunegār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{gunahgār}, \textquotedblleft{}a sinner, an offender\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{gunāh}, the word behind \textbf{\gu{ગુનો}}. It names the person, a man or a woman.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gunegār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gunegār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tyā̃ ajvāḷũ hot to Mīrā gunegārne oḷkhat.} — If there had been light, Mira would have recognized the criminal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to confess, then the Gujarati for to deny, then say \emph{gunegār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ગુનેગાર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A criminal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{જેલ} (jel)}{જેલ (jel)}]{\gu{જેલ} (jel) — a jail}

\label{lesson:GU-C288-jel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to deny, then the Gujarati for a criminal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{જેલ}}
\textbf{\gu{જેલ}} — \emph{jel} — \textquotedblleft{}a jail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ચોર} \gu{હવે} \gu{જેલમાં} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cor have jelmā̃ che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief is in jail now.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{જેલ}} (\emph{jel}) is borrowed from English \emph{jail}. It is feminine: \textbf{\gu{જેલમાં}}, in jail; \textbf{\gu{જેલમાંથી}}, out of jail.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jel}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cor have jelmā̃ che.} — The thief is in jail now.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to deny, then the Gujarati for a criminal, then say \emph{jel} again
\end{itemize}
